reference: GNU coreutils expr (Debian, built with GMP).
coverage: Guest compatibility pass 5 regressions (G74/G83), pass5-keyword-operands, pass5-syntax-and-regex-diagnostics, pass5-bignum-division-and-truth.
Guest pass 6 G97: length, substr, index and ':' count characters in a UTF-8 locale and bytes in C.

cases.purpose: G83: integers of any length (Debian's GMP expr): + - * / % beyond 64 bits; / truncates toward zero, % takes the dividend's sign.
G83: numeric comparison of long integers, leading zeros and -0.
G83: '+ TOKEN' makes TOKEN a string even when it is a keyword or operator; keyword functions take such operands; a bare keyword still needs its operand.
cases.script: expr + match; expr + /; expr length + match; expr + length = + length; { expr + length = length || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'

cases.purpose: G83: division by zero, non-integer argument and a missing operand after + keep GNU's messages and status 2.
cases.script: { expr 1 / 0 || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'; { expr 123456789012345678901234567890 % 0 || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'; { expr a + 1 || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'; { expr + || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'

cases.purpose: G83: keyword functions take primaries as operands (nested keywords, parentheses, + TOKEN); a keyword binds tighter than the operators around it; + quotes ( and ).
cases.script: expr length length abc; expr length '(' abc ')'; expr length 1 + 2; expr length '(' 1 + 2 ')'; expr length + +; expr substr abc + 1 1; expr substr + abc 1 1; expr index + abc c; expr match abc + a; expr + '('; expr '(' + ')' ')'; expr length --; expr -- length abc; expr + -

cases.purpose: G83: GNU's syntax-error wording (missing argument after, expecting ')', unexpected ')' and argument), missing operand with the help hint, and the C library's regex messages, all with status 2.
cases.script: for a in '(' ')' '( 1 + 2' '1 +' '1 2' 'match abc' 'length' 'abc : \(' 'abc : a\{1' '- 1' '-- -- 1' '* * *' '= ='; do set -f; expr $a || echo rc=$?; set +f; done 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'; { expr || echo rc=$?; expr -- || echo rc=$?; } 2>&1 | sed 's/^fixture: line [0-9]*: //'

cases.purpose: G83: exact long division and remainder signs, normalized results, every spelling of zero is false, substr ignores non-integer or out-of-range positions and clamps huge lengths.

G97: in a UTF-8 locale length, substr, index and the ':' match length count characters (a byte that starts no valid sequence is one character, and index matches it only to the same byte); in the C locale they count bytes.
cases.script:
x=$(printf 'a\377b\303')
run() { for e in 'length éa' 'length é€😀' 'substr éab 2 1' 'substr é€😀z 2 2' 'index aé€b €x' 'index éab a' 'é : .' 'é€😀z : .*' 'é€😀z : \(..\)' 'aéb : a.' 'match ééé é*' 'substr éé 2 5' "length $x" "substr $x 2 1" "$x : .*" "index a$(printf '\377')b $(printf '\377')" "index a$(printf '\303')b $(printf '\303\251')" "index é $(printf '\303')" 'substr abc 0 1'; do set -f; r=$(expr $e) && rc=0 || rc=$?; printf '[%s] rc=%s\n' "$r" $rc; set +f; done; }
export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8; echo utf8; run
export LC_ALL=C; echo C; run
